messages:
jason-sales: FYI Craftly (enterprise) reporting high latency this morning even though traffic is low (~5 rps). They say chat p95 jumped from ~400ms to ~2.8s. Trace id they supplied: trace-ccf-20260320-01. Can eng triage? they want ETA for mitigation.

mike-support: I asked for model/route/request_id. Customer sent back: route=/v1/chat, model=redwood-chat-3b-qa, region=us-west2, request_id=rq_8u2x. Attached a short excerpt of their server logs.

jason-sales: Customer is on Dedicated reserved capacity. SLA concerns. They said spike started around 03:12 PDT. No 5xxs, just latency. :eyes:

alice-pm: Can we confirm whether this started after yesterday's runtime deploy (03/19)? If it's Dedicated we should consider fast-track. Need triage: reproduce, root cause, mitigation plan.

ben-runtime: Looking at internal metrics for their workspace: request rate steady low, but batch sizes are tiny and KV cache miss rate ~78% for their prefix pattern. Also runtime prefill times up. No obvious error codes. Pulling the trace now.

carmen-oncall: Pulling trace trace-ccf-20260320-01. Raw timeline shows a 4.1s spike during the aten_matmul call on infra-worker-12 around 03:12:15. GPU utilization on that node is low, but one process shows a long memcpy. Snippet:

```
03:12:15.123 - aten_matmul start pid=4021
03:12:19.276 - memcpy_async wait pid=4021 (stalled 4.15s)
03:12:19.278 - aten_matmul end pid=4021
```

carmen-oncall: Also see repeated tiny batches which would amplify a single stuck op.

sara-sre: infra-worker-12: disk io spike from backup cron at 03:15 (40% IO). Kernel driver for that GPU node is 515.x - there was a noted DMA bug fixed in 520.x drivers. OS logs show a few dma mapping retries.

ben-runtime: If memcpy stalls due to DMA/driver interaction, we can mitigate by routing traffic off that host (rolling drain) or restarting the GPU driver/runtime on the node. Rolling drain preferred to avoid customer impact.

ben-runtime: Can we get an immediate re-route for affected requests? Identify active connections for workspace craftly-org-33 and shift traffic.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: started cordon/drain of infra-worker-12 at 1800010005, rerouting active sessions.

mike-support: Customer confirms p95 improved to ~480ms after we routed them to a different node. They asked to keep them on new host and want RCA + timeline for permanent fix.

alice-pm: OK — prioritize RCA and backfill: "hot-node DMA-driver detection + auto-evict" as a backlog item. Because this is Dedicated and paying, move to high priority and prepare postmortem.

ben-runtime: I'll create a ticket with repro, trace, kernel logs, and suggested runtime patch to detect memcpy stalls (ENG-4567). Mitigation steps in ticket: 1) ride the drain, 2) schedule node reboot/driver update, 3) add a short-circuit for long memcpy to trigger graceful eviction.

carmen-oncall: For immediate monitoring: will add an alert for memcpy stalls >1s and per-node memcpy stall counts.

sara-sre: We'll coordinate with infra to update driver to 520.x on infra-worker-12 family during a low-traffic window. Also verifying that backup cron won't overlap with peak customer windows.

ben-runtime: Created ENG-4567 and linked the trace + logs. Will post the ticket link once available.

mike-support: I'll pass the update to Craftly and schedule a call tomorrow for RCA.

alice-pm: Thanks team. Next steps: (1) postmortem draft under ENG-4567, (2) short-term alert + auto-evict rule, (3) driver rollout plan. Keep updates in thread. :thumbsup:
